scope: Project Claims provider with transactional facts, revision-checked status/confidence, immutable replay receipts, scoped tools and optional Claims UI.
regressions: Project-scoped facts with current Scope read/write roles and authorization before command replay.
Normalized create/update request replay returns the original receipt after later updates or restart; changed operation/input conflicts.
Two real worker threads with separate SQLite connections verify serialized writes and one winning revision comparison.
Borrowed transaction rolls back claim/event/receipt together; final authority check catches source revocation during event persistence.
Original identity and immutable command receipt database guards; all statuses included in stable created-time/ID order.
Same-value accepted update increments revision and records actual prior/current values; authenticated worker or verified user-key provenance.
Flat scalar inputs reject proxies, accessors and nested objects without execution; malformed scalar claim ID is type-checked before schema inspection.
Actual authenticated HTTP/MCP verifies schemas, fixed-session tool grants and claimId argument constraints, source revocation and project isolation.
Cordis removal closes original Claims provider and withdraws its tools/UI row; restoration retains records and avoids duplicate events.
UI retains the same frozen request through later 403/404/409 refusals after an ambiguous earlier outcome, until a successful original receipt resolves it.

correctedPriorProof.problem: The old post-artifact source-revocation regression accepted any rejection; nested transaction refusal happened before revocation and therefore did not test the final authority guard.
correctedPriorProof.correction: Inject same-transaction credential revocation, require the exact authorization refusal, and verify all state rolls back.
correctedPriorProof.mutation: A temporary bundle omitting only final post-artifact Scope.write/Sessions.validate fails the corrected test with Missing expected rejection.
